notes: Science sites: real places worth going to, by body profile id. latitude / longitude in degrees (planetocentric, east-positive), radius in km (the site's extent), value multiplies what experiments there are worth (1 = an ordinary region). factors: how much science a body is worth overall (harder to reach, worth more).

sites.name: Kennedy Space Center
sites.about: Where Apollo left for the Moon.

sites.name: Atacama Desert
sites.about: The driest place on Earth: the soil Mars rovers are tested on.

sites.name: McMurdo Dry Valleys
sites.about: Ice-free Antarctic valleys, as cold and dry as Mars.

sites.name: Meteor Crater
sites.about: A 50,000-year-old impact crater, where Apollo crews trained.

sites.name: Chicxulub
sites.about: The buried crater of the impact that ended the dinosaurs.

sites.name: Tranquility Base
sites.about: Apollo 11's landing site, July 1969.

sites.name: Hadley Rille
sites.about: Apollo 15's site: a lava channel at the foot of the Apennines.

sites.name: Lunar south pole
sites.about: Craters in endless shadow hold water ice (Shackleton, de Gerlache).

sites.name: Tycho
sites.about: A young crater whose rays reach across the near side.

sites.name: Aristarchus
sites.about: The brightest spot on the Moon, on a volcanic plateau.

sites.name: Copernicus
sites.about: A great terraced crater with central peaks of deep crust.

sites.name: Mare Imbrium
sites.about: A vast basin flooded with lava 3.3 billion years ago.

sites.name: South Pole-Aitken basin
sites.about: The Moon's largest and oldest basin, on the far side: its mantle may show.

sites.name: Gale crater
sites.about: An ancient lake bed under Mount Sharp's layered rock (Curiosity).

sites.name: Jezero crater
sites.about: A river delta into an old lake: where Perseverance looks for past life.

sites.name: Olympus Mons
sites.about: The largest volcano in the solar system, 22 km high.

sites.name: Valles Marineris
sites.about: A canyon system 4,000 km long and up to 7 km deep.

sites.name: Hellas Planitia
sites.about: A giant impact basin, the lowest place on Mars: the air is thickest here.

sites.name: Planum Boreum
sites.about: The north polar cap: layered water ice kilometers thick.

sites.name: Meridiani Planum
sites.about: Opportunity's plain, where hematite showed water once soaked the ground.

sites.name: Gusev crater
sites.about: Spirit's crater, with hot-spring silica in its hills.

sites.name: Chryse Planitia
sites.about: Viking 1's landing site, July 1976: outflow channels end here.

sites.name: Utopia Planitia
sites.about: Viking 2's plain, over buried ice.

sites.name: Caloris Planitia
sites.about: A basin 1,550 km across; its impact shook the far side into hills.

sites.name: Mercury's north pole
sites.about: Ice in shadowed craters, closest to the Sun of anywhere.

sites.name: Maxwell Montes
sites.about: Venus's highest mountains, 11 km above the plains.

sites.name: Venera 13 site
sites.about: Where Venera 13 took the first color pictures of the surface (1982).

sites.name: Occator crater
sites.about: Bright salt spots left by brine rising from below.

sites.name: Rheasilvia
sites.about: A crater nearly as wide as Vesta, with a peak 20 km high.

sites.name: Loki Patera
sites.about: A lava lake 200 km across, the most powerful volcano known.

sites.name: Conamara Chaos
sites.about: Rafts of broken ice over the ocean below.

sites.name: Huygens landing site
sites.about: Where the Huygens probe landed on wet ground, January 2005.

sites.name: Kraken Mare
sites.about: A sea of liquid methane and ethane larger than the Caspian.

sites.name: Tiger stripes
sites.about: Fractures venting the ocean beneath into space.

sites.name: Sputnik Planitia
sites.about: A heart-shaped plain of slowly churning nitrogen ice.
